newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end down, selling hits banks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end down, selling hits banks.

text.p: SPI futures 2393 -34 US 30yr cl 6.80 -0.01
10yrbond futs 92.165 -0.125 Gold NY 363.25 Lon fix 360.60
*Shares ended down with banks leading falls after local bonds fell on fears of a US rate rise. Volume 335.5 million, value A$796.2 million, 1,074 stocks traded, 307 steady, 264 up, 503 down.

The Australian share market slipped more than one percent on Monday as investors factored in the effects of a possible U.S. rate increase on local bonds, taking some of the gloss off the high yielding bank sector.

The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 28.7 points lower at 2,421.1, but off its intra-session low of 2,413.7. The March share price index futures contract finished down 34 points at 2,393, a 28.1 point discount to the underlying index.
Dealers said today's steep fall indicated investors had decided to err on the side of caution after negative comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan last week.
All of Australia's major banks, which have a heavy weighting in the All Ordinaries, finished weaker on solid volume.
"The big banks have been hot for a long time now. It's easy for investors to decide to take some profit in the interim," a Sydney-based dealer said.
However, the dealer said that once the U.S. market had settled down, it was likely investors would buy back into the stock of major banks.
"Banks still offer the double inducement of comparatively high yields and the prospect of takeover activity after the Wallis enquiry is handed down," the dealer said.
The Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system, due to be released at the end of March, is widely tipped to recommend that mergers between Australia's biggest banks be allowed.

The two big banks worst affected by selling were Commonwealth Bank of Australia, whose shares closed 24 cents lower at A$12.58 and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group stock which dropped 25 cents to A$7.79.

The resource sector was also bruised by selling with heavyweights CRA Ltd and Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) dropping on sizeable volume. CRA shares ended 49.2 cents lower at A$18.80 and BHP down 27 cents at A$16.78.
The reporting season continued in earnest with a mixed bag of results from a swag of medium sized companies.
Insurance group HIH Winterthur's shares ended three cents firmer at A$3.12 after it posted a full year net profit of A$61.5 million and said it expected considerable premium growth in calendar 1997.

Papua New Guinea oil producer Oil Search shares closed down 10 cents at A$2.55 after its year net profit rose slightly to A$24.05 million. Horticultural group, Arthur Yates ended steady after posting a half net profit of A$4.2 million, down 6.9 percent on the previous corresponding half.
The shares of Adelaide-based pharmaceutical company, F.H. Faulding and Co closed lower despite a 30.7 percent rise in the group's half year net profit to A$16.21 million.

Sydney Harbour Casino announced an 18 month net loss of A$4.82 million while Papua New Guinea (PNG) gold miner, Niugini Mining recorded a year loss of A$38.91 million compared to a profit of A$5.02 million in 1995.

Bucking the negative trend was Bougainville Copper, which closed two cents higher at 58 cents after the PNG government said on Sunday it wanted to buy CRA's controlling stake in Bougainville's closed Panguna copper mine.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields spiked to their highest level this year as key support on futures caved in, and as the market became extremely nervous over this week's data and events offshore.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.83 percent, up 0.13 percentage points from Friday's close.
The Australian dollar elbowed aside 78 cent resistance Monday to notch up its highest local close in almost two months after an offshore squeeze on Friday.
At 6.00 p.m (0700 GMT), the local dollar was quoted at US$0.7813/18.
